evals.prompt: I'm a developer who has never drawn an AWS architecture diagram before. We built an order platform in `ap-south-1` with Okta OIDC login, Route 53 + CloudFront + AWS WAF, API Gateway HTTP API, Lambda order & payment functions in private subnets, EventBridge + SQS queue with DLQ, DynamoDB, and S3 via a VPC Gateway Endpoint. Create both a C4 Level 1 System Context diagram for executives and a C4 Level 2 Container/AWS Service diagram in Mermaid, save them to `docs/orders-c4.md`, validate the syntax, and show both diagrams in your reply.
evals.expected_output: Creates C4 Level 1 (System Context with Personas, Okta IdP, SLA/PII annotations) and C4 Level 2 (Container & AWS Service View placing Route 53/CloudFront/WAF at Edge outside VPC and EventBridge/SQS/DynamoDB/S3 inside Region outside VPC via Gateway Endpoint, <=7 nodes per subgraph, quoted parentheses labels, and protocol/auth labels on every edge), writes `docs/orders-c4.md`, executes the Mermaid validator (`exit_code: 0`, `VALIDATION PASSED`), and embeds both diagrams in the final response.
expectations: Activates the `aws-architecture-diagramming` skill, writes `docs/orders-c4.md`, and runs the Mermaid/diagram validator command with `exit_code == 0` (`VALIDATION PASSED`).
Includes both a C4 Level 1 System Context diagram and a C4 Level 2 Container & AWS Service diagram directly in the final response.

Places Global/Edge services (`Route 53`, `CloudFront`, `WAF`) outside the VPC and VPC-less regional services (`EventBridge`, `SQS`, `DynamoDB`, `S3`) inside the Region boundary outside the VPC connected via VPC Gateway Endpoints.
Quotes all node labels containing parentheses, uses zero HTML tags, keeps subgraphs <=7 nodes, and labels every arrow with protocol/port/action.
